# backend-process-implementation

Orchestration layer for all Power Automate Cloud Flow work in this project.
The `power-automate` plugin covers the full flow lifecycle from discovery through production.

## Step 0 — Dependency preflight (required)

Before routing any flow task, verify `power-automate` sub-skills are available:
`setup`, `browse-flows`, `create-flow`, `build-flow`, `debug-flow`, `diagnose-flow`,
`manage-flows`, `manage-desktop-flows`, and `route-environments`.

If any required sub-skill is missing or unavailable:
1. Stop execution and return a blocked status.
2. Ask the user whether they want to install or enable the missing dependency.
3. Resume only after availability is confirmed.

Do not attempt flow authoring or diagnosis through ad-hoc JSON edits when these dependencies
are missing.

## Step 1 — Environment and solution scope gate (required)

Before any flow work starts, require explicit target scope:
- Environment: display name and environment ID (or URL)
- Solution: unique name and publisher prefix

If either environment or solution is missing, ambiguous, or inferred:
1. Stop execution and return a blocked status.
2. Ask the user to explicitly provide the target environment and solution.
3. Resume only after both are confirmed.

Do not create, modify, diagnose, or enable flows against an implicit target.

## Available sub-skills

| Sub-skill | When to use |
|-----------|-------------|
| `setup` | First-time environment configuration for Power Automate |
| `browse-flows` | Discover existing flows before creating new ones |
| `create-flow` | Scaffold a new solution-bound cloud flow |
| `build-flow` | Add actions, conditions, and logic to a flow |
| `debug-flow` | Interactively diagnose a failing or misbehaving flow |
| `diagnose-flow` | Automated root-cause analysis on a failed run |
| `manage-flows` | Enable, disable, delete, and update flow metadata |
| `manage-desktop-flows` | Manage RPA / desktop flows |
| `route-environments` | Resolve and switch the active Power Platform environment |

## Source of truth for the flow backlog

Before scaffolding a new flow, consult `ARCHITECTURE.md` §3–4 (Submission review flow;
Non-AI backend processes) at the repo root — it enumerates the flows this product needs
(submission review orchestration, geocoding, fun facts generation, nightly leaderboard
computation, season rollover, winner announcement notification), their triggers, and which
call a Copilot Studio agent via **Execute Agent and wait**. Treat it as the flow backlog
rather than re-deriving requirements from an ad hoc request.

## Project conventions

### 1 — Solution-bound flows only
Every flow must be created inside a Dataverse solution.
Standalone flows (not inside a solution) are not committed to this repo.
When creating a flow, always pass the solution name to `create-flow`.

### 2 — Naming convention
All flows must follow: `<SolutionPrefix>_<VerbObject>`

Examples (replace `MCDM` with the actual solution publisher prefix once confirmed — see the
scope gate in Step 1; these are illustrative only and don't reflect the Poutine League domain):
- `MCDM_NotifyOnCaseCreated`
- `MCDM_ProcessApprovalResponse`
- `MCDM_SyncContactToSharePoint`

Reject or rename flows that do not match this pattern before pushing to a solution.

### 3 — Connection references
Connection references must **not** be hardcoded in flow definitions.
They belong in `solutions/<solution-name>/deployment-settings.json`.
When `build-flow` or `create-flow` surfaces a connection reference, record it in
`deployment-settings.json` rather than embedding it inline.

### 4 — Check before creating
Before scaffolding any new flow, run `browse-flows` to check for existing flows with
overlapping trigger/purpose. Surface any potential duplicates to the user before proceeding.
Duplicate flows in a solution cause confusion and inflate licensing costs.

### 5 — Diagnose before fixing
When a flow fails in any environment, always run `diagnose-flow` first.
Do not attempt to fix a flow based on symptom description alone — the diagnostic output
often reveals a different root cause than the surface error.

### 6 — Production enable requires human approval
Before enabling (turning on) any flow in a **production environment**:
1. Present the flow name, solution, trigger, and estimated run frequency.
2. **Wait for explicit human approval.**

This applies even in autopilot mode. Do not self-approve production enables.

## Standard workflow

```
New flow request
  └─ Dependency preflight
       ├─ Missing dependency? → ask to install/enable → stop until resolved
       └─ Scope gate (environment + solution explicit)
            ├─ Missing or ambiguous? → ask user → stop until resolved
            └─ browse-flows (check for duplicates)
                 └─ create-flow (solution-bound, MCDM_ naming)
                      └─ build-flow (add logic)
                           └─ manage-flows:test run
                                └─ Production? → confirm human → manage-flows:enable
```

```
Broken flow
  └─ Dependency preflight
       ├─ Missing dependency? → ask to install/enable → stop until resolved
       └─ Scope gate (environment + solution explicit)
            ├─ Missing or ambiguous? → ask user → stop until resolved
            └─ diagnose-flow (always first)
                 └─ Identify root cause
                      └─ build-flow or manage-flows to fix
                           └─ Re-test → manage-flows:enable (if production, confirm first)
```

## Escape hatches

- If the target environment is unclear, run `route-environments` before any other sub-skill.
- If `diagnose-flow` returns an auth error, route to `data-management` skill to check
  connection references via `dv-connect` before re-running diagnostics.
- Desktop / RPA flows → `manage-desktop-flows` instead of `manage-flows`.

</skill-context>

133. ### Security roles
134. 
135. - **Admin/Moderator**: a small group (2–3 people) using the built-in **System Administrator** security role — acceptable at this scale/org, keeps setup simple, no custom role needed.
136. - **Employee**: follows the **principle of least privilege** — read access to all public data (submissions, reviews, leaderboards), write access scoped to their own submissions/tries/reviews only. Exact field- and record-level privileges to be defined as a custom security role when building the code apps.
137. 
138. ### Confirmed decisions
139. 
140. - **Restaurant stays normalized as its own table** (as modeled above) — gives a cleaner data model, clear separation of concerns per table, and enables future capabilities like tracking which restaurants keep appearing across seasons.
141. - **`Season Result` stores a full ranked-list snapshot per season/category**, not just the top-1 winner — even though only the top-1 is announced/crowned at season close, the fuller snapshot supports richer leaderboard history and analytics later.
142. - **The ranked-entries list is implemented as a child table, `Season Result Entry`** (lookup to Season Result, rank, score, and *either* an employee lookup *or* a Poutine Submission lookup depending on the category's computation type) — since Dataverse cannot store an array inside a single row. This is a relational-decomposition implementation detail of the `Season Result` row above, not new business scope.
143. 
144. > [!NOTE]
145. > The `Season Result Entry` child table was introduced autonomously by an agent session in the human's absence, to make the "ranked entries" concept concrete in Dataverse. Flagged here for human review — a different representation (e.g. JSON blob, fixed top-N columns) can still be adopted if preferred.

147. ## 2. AI agentic experiences (Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot harness)
148. 
149. All Copilot Studio agents in this product are built on the **[GitHub Copilot harness](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/harnesses-overview)** (no classic "topics" — reasoning-driven, tool/knowledge/connected-agent orchestration).
150. 
151. ### 2.1 Interactive conversational agent (single entry point)
152. 
153. One agent serves as the **single conversational entry point** for employees — submitting/managing poutines, exploring poutines to try, and checking the leaderboard, all through natural-language interaction. It is:
154. 
155. - **Embedded inside the employee-facing code app** (chat panel), and
156. - **Also published standalone to Microsoft 365 Copilot**,
157. 
158. so employees can reach it from either surface. It uses Dataverse as a tool/knowledge source to read and write submissions, tries, and reviews on the user's behalf, respecting the same security roles as the code app.
159. 
160. ### 2.2 Specialized backend agents (headless, non-interactive)
161. 
162. Backend AI reasoning is split into **specialized agents**, each with a narrow responsibility, invoked as backend processes rather than through chat:
163. 
164. | Backend agent | Responsibility | Triggered by |
165. |---|---|---|
166. | **Submission Review agent** | Combines completeness check, duplicate/similarity detection (same restaurant/very similar poutine), and first-pass moderation; escalates ambiguous cases instead of deciding blindly. | Poutine Submission status change `Draft` → `Submitted` (see [submission flow](#3-submission-review-flow)). |
167. | **Fun Facts agent** | Generates engaging trivia/context about an approved poutine or restaurant, grounded in Dataverse data (submission details, tags, restaurant info) and the model's general knowledge — **no external web search grounding**, to keep the demo self-contained. | Poutine Submission reaching `Approved` status; may also be reused on-demand as a connected-agent tool by the interactive agent when an employee asks for a fun fact in chat. |
168. | **Review Quality agent** | Scores review helpfulness/insightfulness to power the "Best Critic" category. | Nightly leaderboard computation flow (§4). |
169. 
170. > [!NOTE]
171. > **Multi-agent design follows Microsoft's guidance**: keep it to one interactive agent as the default entry point, and only split into specialized agents where there's a distinct domain, distinct trigger, or reusability need — which is the case for review, fun facts, and review-quality scoring.
172. 
173. ## 3. Submission review flow
174. 
175. 1. An employee starts a **Poutine Submission** in `Draft` status via the employee code app (or the conversational agent).
176. 2. When ready, they move it to `Submitted`.
177. 3. The **Submission Review agent** is invoked from a **Power Automate cloud flow** triggered on that Dataverse status change, and performs completeness + duplicate/similarity + first-pass moderation checks.
178. 4. Clear-cut outcomes move the record straight to `Approved` or `Rejected`.
179. 5. Ambiguous cases are flagged `In Review` and escalated to a human moderator/admin.
180. 
181. ### Escalation mechanism (open question — see below)
182. 
183. - **Primary (aspirational)**: use Copilot Studio's **[Request for Information (RFI)](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/blog/copilot-studio/introducing-request-for-information-in-copilot-studio-agent-flows/)** human-in-the-loop node inside a **Copilot Studio Workflow**, emailing the moderator a structured form and feeding the response back into the flow.
184. - **Fallback (primary for the demo)**: flag the Dataverse record `In Review`, surface it in the **admin code app**'s review queue, and send a lightweight **Microsoft Teams heads-up notification** via Power Automate.
185. 
186. > [!IMPORTANT]
187. > Copilot Studio **Workflows** are not yet supported by the Copilot Studio-related skills/plugins used in this repo (`skills-for-copilot-studio`, `copilot-studio-plugin`). Until that changes, **Power Automate cloud flows call specialized Copilot Studio agents directly** via the **[Microsoft Copilot Studio connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/microsoftcopilotstudio/)** as the one consistent AI-invocation pattern across the product. Adopting Copilot Studio Workflows (and the RFI node) for the submission-review escalation is a **future exploration to keep an eye on** as Microsoft's tooling evolves — it is not expected to land in time for this demo.
188.

1. # Dev environment & solution conventions
2. 
3. This document is the source of truth for the **human-chosen, stable names** used by the
4. Poutine League Dev solution. System-generated GUIDs (environment ID/URL, solution ID) are
5. **not** stored here — they live in GitHub repository variables (see below) because they are
6. instance-specific and never chosen by us.
7. 
8. ## Stable names (safe to commit)
9. 
10. | Concept | Value |
11. |---|---|
12. | Publisher display name | Raphael Pothin |
13. | Publisher unique name | `rpothin` |
14. | Publisher prefix | `rpo` |
15. | Solution display name | Poutine League Core |
16. | Solution unique name | `poutineleaguecore` |
17. | Local solution folder | `solutions/poutineleaguecore/` |
18. 
19. > [!NOTE]
20. > The publisher prefix (`rpo`) is effectively permanent — every custom table, column, and
21. > relationship created under this solution keeps this prefix forever, even if the publisher
22. > is changed later. Never mix prefixes within the same solution.
23. 
24. ## System-generated GUIDs (GitHub repository variables)
25. 
26. These are stored as [GitHub repository variables](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/learn-github-actions/variables)
27. on `rpothin/mcdm26-ai-native-powerplatform-dev` — never committed to tracked files.
28. 
29. | Variable | Meaning | Consumed by |
30. |---|---|---|
31. | `DEV_ENVIRONMENT_URL` | Dev environment org URL | `pac`, `dataverse` CLI, `dv-solution`/`dv-connect` skills |
32. | `DEV_ENVIRONMENT_ID` | Dev environment ID (GUID) | Power Automate `flowagent`/`route-environments` tooling |
33. | `DEV_SOLUTION_ID` | `solutionid` GUID for `poutineleaguecore` | Any tooling that needs the solution record directly (vs. by unique name) |
34. 
35. Resolve them in any session with:
36. 
37. ```powershell
38. gh variable get DEV_ENVIRONMENT_URL --repo rpothin/mcdm26-ai-native-powerplatform-dev
39. gh variable get DEV_ENVIRONMENT_ID  --repo rpothin/mcdm26-ai-native-powerplatform-dev

44. 
45. A `dv-connect`-managed `.env` (gitignored) and `scripts/auth.py` (committed) provide Dataverse
46. SDK/CLI/MCP access for a given developer's machine. `.env` is per-machine and re-derivable from
47. the values in this document plus the GitHub variables above — never commit it.
48. 
49. ## Versioning ([Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/))
50. 
51. The `poutineleaguecore` solution version follows SemVer. Dataverse's solution version format
52. (`Major.Minor.Build`) maps 1:1 onto SemVer's `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` — no reserved or padded
53. segment needed.
54. 
55. | SemVer | Dataverse segment | Bump when |
56. |---|---|---|
57. | `MAJOR` | Major | Breaking change — removed/renamed component, breaking schema change |
58. | `MINOR` | Minor | New backward-compatible feature — new table, column, flow, agent, app |
59. | `PATCH` | Build (3rd segment) | Backward-compatible fix |
60. 
61. Current version: `1.0.0` (initial release — MAJOR=1, MINOR=0, PATCH=0).

63. Bump the version **in the Dev environment first** (source of truth for the live solution

65. change — never hand-edit that file directly:

2. # Targets operate on directories discovered at runtime so no file changes are needed when

3. description: >
4.   Orchestrates Power Platform solution lifecycle in the Dev environment for a Power Platform
5.   project. Covers solution creation, local clone and sync, semantic-versioned solution version

8.   starting any content work session or when a pre-PR quality gate is needed. Triggers on:
9.   create solution, clone solution, sync solution, bump solution version, semver, semantic
10.   versioning, solution checker, pack solution, deployment settings, generate settings,
11.   connection references, environment variables, solution hygiene, dependency check,
12.   pre-PR validation, init solution. Do NOT use for: deploying or importing solutions to
13.   staging or production (use the GitHub deployment workflow), creating Dataverse tables or
14.   records (use data-management), building flows (use backend-process-implementation),

17. 
18. # solution-management
19. 
20. Orchestration layer for Power Platform solution lifecycle in the Dev environment.
21. This skill owns the solution *container* — creating it, keeping local files current,
22. generating configuration artifacts, and validating quality before a PR. It does **not**
23. deploy solutions to higher environments; that boundary is owned by the GitHub workflow.
24. 
25. ## Step 0 — Dependency preflight (required)
26. 
27. Before any solution work, verify the primary sub-skill is available:
28. - `dv-solution` from the `dataverse` plugin (microsoft/Dataverse-skills)
29. 
30. If `dv-solution` is unavailable, check for `pac` CLI as fallback:
31. - Run `pac --version` to confirm availability.
32. 
33. If neither is available:
34. 1. Stop execution and return a blocked status.
35. 2. Ask the user whether they want to install or enable the missing dependency.
36. 3. Resume only after at least one option is confirmed.
37. 
38. Tool priority for all operations in this skill:
39. 1. `dv-solution` sub-skill (preferred — higher-level, safer, plugin-managed)
40. 2. `pac` CLI (fallback — when `dv-solution` does not cover the operation)
41. 3. Raw Power Platform API / `az` CLI (last resort only — flag explicitly before using)
42. 
43. ## Step 1 — Environment and solution scope gate (required)
44. 
45. Before any solution work starts, require explicit target scope:
46. - Environment: Dev environment display name and environment ID (or URL)
47. - Solution: unique name and publisher prefix
48. 
49. If either is missing, ambiguous, or inferred:
50. 1. Stop execution and return a blocked status.
51. 2. Ask the user to explicitly provide the Dev target environment and solution.
52. 3. Resume only after both are confirmed.
53. 
54. Only the Dev environment is a valid target for agent-driven solution work. Any request
55. targeting staging or production must be rejected — point the user to the GitHub workflow.
56. 
57. ## Source of truth for ALM strategy
58. 
59. `ARCHITECTURE.md` §7 (ALM & environments) at the repo root confirms the current strategy for
60. this project: a **single Dev environment with one unmanaged solution** holding all components
61. (tables, flows, code apps, agents). Use it to pre-fill the scope gate above instead of
62. re-negotiating environment/solution scope from scratch each session — but still have the user
63. confirm the exact environment ID/URL and solution unique name before any write. The repo's
64. `.github/workflows/deploy-solution.yml` illustrates the target multi-environment promotion
65. pattern but is explicitly out of scope for live agent-driven work (see Hard boundaries below).
66. 
67. ## Operations and tool routing
68. 
69. ### Solution creation
70. 
71. Goal: ensure the solution exists in the Dev environment with the correct publisher and prefix.
72. 
73. 1. Use `dv-solution` to check whether the solution already exists.
74. 2. If it does not exist, use `dv-solution` to create it (publisher + prefix required).
75. 3. If `dv-solution` cannot create directly, fall back to `pac solution create` CLI.
76. 
77. ### Local clone and sync
78. 
79. Goal: keep local solution files current with the Dev environment state.
80. 
81. - First clone: `dv-solution` export + unpack, or `pac solution clone` as fallback.
82. - Subsequent sync: `dv-solution` pull / sync operation, or `pac solution sync` as fallback.
83. - Solution files live under `solutions/<solution-unique-name>/` at the repo root.
84. - Never manually edit files under `solutions/<solution-unique-name>/Other/` — they are
85.   managed by the tooling.
86. 
87. ### Solution versioning ([Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/))
88. 
89. Goal: keep the solution's version meaningful and monotonically increasing, using SemVer
90. semantics. Dataverse's solution version format (`Major.Minor.Build`) maps 1:1 onto SemVer's
91. `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` — no reserved or padded segment needed.
92. 
93. | SemVer | Dataverse segment | Bump when |
94. |---|---|---|
95. | `MAJOR` | Major | Breaking change — removed/renamed component, breaking schema change |
96. | `MINOR` | Minor | New backward-compatible feature — new table, column, flow, agent, app |
97. | `PATCH` | Build (3rd segment) | Backward-compatible fix |
98. 
99. **Bump the version in the Dev environment (source of truth), then re-sync locally** —
100. never hand-edit `Other/Solution.xml` directly (it is tooling-managed, see Local clone and
101. sync above):
102. 
103. 1. `dv-solution` — use if it exposes a version-bump operation.
104. 2. `pac solution online-version --environment <url> --solution-name <UniqueName> --solution-version <Major.Minor.Patch>` — primary fallback (CLI). Omit `--solution-version` to read the current online version.
105. 3. Re-sync/re-export the solution so the local unpacked `Other/Solution.xml` reflects the new version.
106. 
107. Bump the version as part of any change that introduces a new component or a fix, before
108. running the solution checker / pack step of the pre-PR quality gate. Ask the user to confirm
109. the bump level (major/minor/patch) whenever it isn't obvious from the change.
110. 
111. ### Deployment-settings generation
112. 
113. Goal: produce `solutions/<solution-unique-name>/deployment-settings.json` containing all
114. connection references and environment variable definitions, with placeholder values for
115. non-Dev environments.
116. 
117. 1. `dv-solution` — use if it exposes a settings-generation operation.
118. 2. `pac solution generate-settings` — primary fallback (CLI).
119. 3. Manual inspection of the unpacked solution XML — last resort; flag to user.
120. 
121. After generation, verify every connection reference and environment variable in the solution
122. has a corresponding entry. Surface any gaps to the user before proceeding.
123. 
124. ### Solution checker
125. 
126. Goal: validate the solution against Power Platform best-practice rules before a PR.
127. 
128. 1. `dv-solution` — use if it exposes a checker operation.
129. 2. `pac solution check` — primary fallback (CLI).
130. 
131. Always run with the standard ruleset. Surface all Critical and High severity findings to
132. the user and block the PR recommendation until they are addressed or explicitly waived.
133. 
134. ### Solution pack (pre-PR artifact)
135. 
136. Goal: produce a clean `.zip` pack of the local solution for CI consumption.
137. 
138. 1. `dv-solution` — use if it exposes a pack operation.
139. 2. `pac solution pack` — primary fallback (CLI).
140. 
141. Pack is the last step before opening a PR. Never pack a solution that has failing checker
142. results (Critical/High) unless the user has explicitly waived them.
143. 
144. ### Dependency hygiene
145. 
146. Goal: identify and flag dependency risks in the solution before changes are committed.
147. 
148. Check for:
149. - Components that depend on managed solutions not listed as explicit dependencies
150. - Circular or implicit dependencies between solutions in the same publisher
151. - Unmanaged customisations layered on top of managed components
152. 
153. Use `dv-solution` introspection first; fall back to inspecting the unpacked solution XML.
154. Surface findings as warnings — do not auto-fix dependency issues without human guidance.
155. 
156. ## Standard workflows
157. 
158. ```
159. Start of a feature session
160.   └─ Step 0: dependency preflight
161.        └─ Step 1: scope gate (Dev env + solution explicit)
162.             ├─ Solution missing in Dev? → create (dv-solution → pac fallback)
163.             └─ Solution exists
164.                  ├─ Not cloned locally? → clone (dv-solution → pac fallback)
165.                  └─ Already cloned? → sync (dv-solution → pac fallback)
166.                       └─ deployment-settings.json current? → generate if not
167.                            └─ Hand off to content skills (data / agent / app / flow)
168. ```
169. 
170. ```
171. Pre-PR quality gate
172.   └─ Sync (pull latest Dev state)
173.        └─ deployment-settings.json up to date? → regenerate if not
174.             └─ Version bump needed? → bump SemVer (online-version → re-sync)
175.                  └─ solution checker (dv-solution → pac fallback)
176.                       ├─ Critical/High findings? → block → surface to user
177.                       └─ Clean (or waived) → pac solution pack
178.                            └─ Ready for PR
179. ```
180. 
181. ## Hard boundaries
182. 
183. | Action | Status | Reason |
184. |--------|--------|--------|
185. | `pac solution import` / `dv-solution` import to staging/prod | **Forbidden** | Deployment is the GitHub workflow |
186. | Write operations targeting non-Dev environments | **Forbidden** | Dev only for agent-driven work |
187. | Auto-fixing dependency issues | **Blocked** | Requires human guidance |
188. | Packing with unresolved Critical/High checker findings | **Blocked** | Unless user explicitly waives |
189.

191. 
192. - If `dv-solution` and `pac` both fail for an operation, surface the raw error + the
193.   manual XML-based fallback steps rather than attempting a raw API call silently.
194. - If the solution has multiple layers (managed base + unmanaged top), document which layer
195.   is being operated on before any export or pack.
196. - If `deployment-settings.json` already exists and is more recent than the last sync,

1. # deploy-solution.yml
2. #
3. # PURPOSE
4. # -------
5. # Deploys updated Power Platform solutions to the production environment
6. # whenever changes to `solutions/**` are pushed to the `main` branch.
7. # Each changed solution is packed from its unpacked folder and imported
8. # via the PAC CLI using an OIDC-based auth flow (no long-lived secrets).
9. #
10. # AZURE AD SETUP REQUIRED
11. # -----------------------
12. # 1. Create an App Registration in Azure AD (Entra ID).
13. # 2. Under "Certificates & secrets → Federated credentials", add a credential:
14. #      - Scenario : GitHub Actions deploying Azure resources
15. #      - Organization: rpothin
16. #      - Repository : mcdm26-ai-native-powerplatform-dev
17. #      - Entity     : Branch
18. #      - Branch name: main
19. #    This allows the workflow to exchange the GitHub OIDC token for an Azure
20. #    access token without storing a client secret anywhere.
21. # 3. Grant the App Registration access to the target Power Platform environment
22. #    (System Administrator or equivalent security role).
23. #
24. # REPOSITORY SECRETS (Settings → Secrets → Actions)
25. # ---------------------------------------------------
26. #   AZURE_CLIENT_ID       – Application (client) ID of the App Registration
27. #   AZURE_TENANT_ID       – Azure AD tenant ID
28. #   AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID – Azure subscription ID
29. #
30. # REPOSITORY VARIABLES (Settings → Variables → Actions)
31. # ------------------------------------------------------
32. #   PROD_ENVIRONMENT_URL  – Production Power Platform environment URL
33. #                           e.g. https://org1234abcd.crm.dynamics.com
34. #
35. # DEPLOYMENT SETTINGS PER SOLUTION
36. # ---------------------------------
37. # Each solution folder must contain a `deployment-settings.json` file that
38. # maps environment-specific connection references and environment variables.
39. # Generate a template from an existing packed zip:
40. #   pac solution create-settings --solution-zip <file>.zip --settings-file deployment-settings.json
41. 
42. on:
43.   push:
44.     branches: [main]
45.     paths: ['solutions/**']
46. 
47. jobs:
48.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
49.   # Job 1: detect — find which solution folders changed in this push
50.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
51.   detect:
52.     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
53.     permissions:
54.       contents: read
55.     outputs:
56.       solutions: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.solutions }}
57. 
58.     steps:
59.       - name: Checkout
60.         uses: actions/checkout@v4
61.         with:
62.           fetch-depth: 2  # Need HEAD and HEAD~1 to compute the diff
63. 
64.       - name: Detect changed solutions
65.         id: changed
66.         run: |
67.           # List files that changed between the previous commit and this one,
68.           # filter to paths inside solutions/, extract the solution name (second
69.           # path segment), deduplicate, then encode as a JSON array.
70.           CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD -- 'solutions/' \
71.             | sed 's|solutions/\([^/]*\)/.*|\1|' \
72.             | sort -u)
73. 
74.           if [ -z "$CHANGED" ]; then
75.             echo "solutions=[]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
76.           else
77.             # Build a JSON array from the newline-delimited list.
78.             JSON=$(echo "$CHANGED" | jq -R . | jq -sc .)
79.             echo "solutions=$JSON" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
80.           fi
81. 
82.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
83.   # Job 2: deploy — pack and import each changed solution
84.   # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
85.   deploy:
86.     needs: detect
87.     if: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.solutions != '[]' && needs.detect.outputs.solutions != '' }}
88.     # Queue imports for this workflow/environment to avoid concurrent solution
89.     # deployments, which can fail due to Power Platform import-side locking.
90.     concurrency:
91.       group: powerplatform-prod-solution-deploy
92.       cancel-in-progress: false
93. 
94.     strategy:
95.       matrix:
96.         solution: ${{ fromJson(needs.detect.outputs.solutions) }}
97.       fail-fast: false  # Let independent solutions proceed even if one fails
98. 
99.     environment: production  # Enables GitHub environment protection rules
100.     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
101.     permissions:
102.       id-token: write  # Required for OIDC token exchange with Azure AD
103.       contents: write  # Required for gh release create/edit/delete
104. 
105.     steps:
106.       - name: Checkout
107.         uses: actions/checkout@v4
108. 
109.       - name: Install PAC CLI
110.         uses: microsoft/powerplatform-actions/install-pac-cli@v1
111. 
112.       - name: Create release candidate
113.         id: create_release
114.         env:
115.           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
116.         run: |
117.           SHORT_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
118.           TAG="${{ matrix.solution }}-v${SHORT_SHA}-rc"
119.           gh release create "$TAG" \
120.             --prerelease \
121.             --title "${{ matrix.solution }} RC-${SHORT_SHA}" \
122.             --notes "Automated release candidate for ${{ matrix.solution }}"
123.           echo "tag=$TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
124. 
125.       - name: Pack solution
126.         run: |
127.           mkdir -p dist
128.           pac solution pack \
129.             --folder "solutions/${{ matrix.solution }}" \
130.             --zipfile "dist/${{ matrix.solution }}.zip" \
131.             --processCanvasApps
132. 
133.       - name: Validate deployment settings file
134.         shell: bash
135.         run: |
136.           settings="solutions/${{ matrix.solution }}/deployment-settings.json"
137.           if [ ! -f "$settings" ]; then
138.             echo "ERROR: deployment-settings.json not found for solution '${{ matrix.solution }}'."
139.             echo "Generate it with 'make solution-sync SOLUTION=${{ matrix.solution }}' before pushing."
140.             exit 1
141.           fi
142. 
143.       - name: Azure login (OIDC)
144.         uses: azure/login@v2
145.         with:
146.           client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
147.           tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
148.           subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
149. 
150.       - name: Authenticate PAC CLI
151.         run: |
152.           # Exchange the Azure session token for a Power Platform-scoped token,
153.           # then register the auth context so subsequent pac commands target the
154.           # correct environment without storing credentials in the workflow.
155.           TOKEN=$(az account get-access-token \
156.             --resource "https://service.powerapps.com/" \
157.             --query accessToken -o tsv)
158.           pac auth create \
159.             --environment "${{ vars.PROD_ENVIRONMENT_URL }}" \
160.             --token "$TOKEN"
161. 
162.       - name: Import solution
163.         id: import
164.         continue-on-error: false
165.         run: |
166.           pac solution import \
167.             --path "dist/${{ matrix.solution }}.zip" \
168.             --deploymentSettingsFile "solutions/${{ matrix.solution }}/deployment-settings.json" \
169.             --activate-plugins \
170.             --force-overwrite \
171.             --publish-changes
172. 
173.       - name: Promote release on success
174.         if: steps.import.outcome == 'success'
175.         env:
176.           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
177.         run: |
178.           TAG="${{ steps.create_release.outputs.tag }}"
179.           gh release edit "$TAG" --prerelease=false --latest
180. 
181.       # NOTE: This rollback only removes the GitHub release and tag.
182.       # It does NOT revert the Power Platform environment to its previous state.
183.       # If the import partially succeeded, the environment may be in an inconsistent state.
184.       # Manual intervention (re-importing the previous solution version) may be required.
185.       - name: Rollback release on failure
186.         if: failure() && steps.create_release.outcome == 'success'
187.         env:
188.           GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
189.         run: |
190.           TAG="${{ steps.create_release.outputs.tag }}"
191.           gh release delete "$TAG" --yes
192.           # Remove the tag from the remote; ignore errors if it was never pushed.
193.           git push origin --delete "$TAG" || true

30. 
31. - Submit a poutine (restaurant/place name + address, poutine name/description, price, photo, tags) — hard cap of **5 active submissions** per employee.
32. - New submissions go through lightweight AI-assisted first-pass moderation and a duplicate/similarity check before becoming publicly visible; ambiguous cases are escalated to human moderators via the separate admin app (not built here).
33. - "Trying" a poutine is self-declared (honor system, no proof required) and precedes leaving a review.
34. - A review is a star rating (1–5) plus a short written comment; reviews/ratings are visible to everyone, tied to the reviewer's real name.
35. - Discovery via a filterable list/feed (tags, neighborhood, rating) and a map view.
36. - Four launch leaderboard categories — Best Seller, Top Poutine (confidence-weighted rating), Best Supporter, Best Critic — tracked as both an all-time Hall of Fame and per-season (winter/spring/summer/autumn) standings.
37. - Notifications are intentionally minimal — season/category winner announcements only; day-to-day activity (someone trying your poutine, new reviews) is discovered by browsing, not pushed.

+# Scheduled Leaderboard Snapshot
+
+## Problem and approach
+
+Add a solution-bound Power Automate cloud flow that runs nightly at 02:00
+America/Toronto and refreshes the active season's durable leaderboard snapshots
+for the three deterministic launch categories: Best Seller, Top Poutine, and
+Best Supporter. The flow will use Dataverse aggregate queries, update one
+`Season Result` per active-season/category pair, replace its child entries
+idempotently, and preserve the complete ranked list.
+
+The work stays on the current feature branch and lands in one PR. It will use
+the Power Automate and solution-management skills rather than hand-authored
+flow JSON or hand-edited generated solution XML.
+
+## Scope decisions
+
+- Target: repository-defined Dev environment (`DEV_ENVIRONMENT_URL` /
+  `DEV_ENVIRONMENT_ID`), solution `poutineleaguecore`, publisher prefix `rpo`.
+- Flow name: `rpo_CreateScheduledLeaderboardSnapshot`.
+- Trigger: Power Automate Recurrence, once daily at 02:00
+  America/Toronto.
+- Categories: `try_count_by_submitter`, `weighted_rating`, and
+  `try_count_by_employee`. `review_helpfulness_score` / Best Critic is
+  explicitly deferred and requires a future Review Quality agent prerequisite.
+- Top Poutine: documented Bayesian weighted average using the global mean and
+  minimum review count `m = 3`; define deterministic tie-breaking before
+  authoring.
+- Snapshot shape: one header per active-season/category, all ranked entries,
+  `ComputedAt` set on each run, and replacement of prior child entries to make
+  reruns idempotent.
+
+## Implementation todos
+
+1. Confirm the live Dev solution and flow inventory; check for duplicate or
+   overlapping leaderboard flows before authoring.
+2. Verify prerequisite Dataverse data and permissions: an active `Season`, the
+   three seeded `Category` rows and computation types, source-table access, and
+   a flow owner/service connection with read/write rights for Season, Category,
+   Try, Review, Poutine Submission, Season Result, Season Result Entry, and
+   SystemUser lookups.
+3. Manually ensure a connected Microsoft Dataverse connection reference exists
+   in the live unmanaged solution and is mapped to an authenticated Dev
+   connection. The Power Automate authoring skill can create/use the reference
+   but cannot replace this live maker/admin authorization step.
+4. Author the solution-bound recurrence flow through the flow skills:
+   active-season/category discovery, FetchXML/Dataverse aggregates, Bayesian
+   Top Poutine calculation, deterministic sorting/ranking, header upsert,
+   child-entry cleanup and recreation, pagination, sequential writes, and
+   explicit failure handling.
+5. Generate/refresh `solutions/poutineleaguecore/deployment-settings.json`
+   from the final solution contents, verify every connection reference is
+   represented, and keep live connection IDs/secrets out of tracked files.
+6. Test the flow in Dev with seeded data, including a second run to prove
+   idempotency, exact three-category coverage, full ranking persistence,
+   no Best Critic writes, and a surfaced failure path.
+7. Read the online solution version first. Because a new backward-compatible
+   flow is a MINOR change, bump `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` from the live version to
+   `MAJOR.(MINOR+1).0` (expected `1.10.0` if the live version is `1.9.0`).
+   Use `pac solution online-version` against Dev, never edit
+   `Other/Solution.xml`, then re-sync/export so the unpacked manifest records
+   the live version.
+8. Run the repository solution gate (pack plus Solution Checker), address or
+   surface Critical/High findings, and inspect the final diff for only flow,
+   deployment-settings, and generated solution changes. Do not update
+   `PRODUCT.md` or `ARCHITECTURE.md` in this implementation without a separate
+   explicit approval; the deferred Best Critic decision should remain visible
+   as a follow-up.
+9. As the final ALM step, export the unmanaged `poutineleaguecore` solution
+   from Dev with PAC CLI to an ignored `dist/poutineleaguecore_<version>.zip`,
+   verify the exported manifest/version and included flow, and leave no
+   environment-specific artifact tracked by Git.
+10. Capture Entire observability, perform the repository's dry-link/apply and
+    stack-finalize protocol, then open the single PR from this branch.
+
+## Manual prerequisites and handoffs
+
+- Authenticate PAC/Power Platform tooling if the session has no active Dev
+  context; do not substitute production or staging.
+- In the Dev solution, select or create the Dataverse connection reference and
+  bind it to a connected account with the required table privileges. Confirm
+  the flow owner is allowed to use that connection.
+- Confirm the active season and category seed data exist before the first
+  scheduled run; otherwise the flow should fail visibly or create no
+  misleading snapshot rather than silently succeeding.
+- Best Critic is intentionally out of scope for this PR. A future change must
+  publish the Review Quality Copilot Studio agent, add its connection
+  reference, and extend the flow with `Execute Agent and wait`.
+- Solution versioning and final export require a Dev user/service principal
+  with solution read/write/export permissions; these are live-environment
+  permissions, not repository changes.
+
+## Notes
+
+- The checked-in manifest currently shows `1.9.0`, while the conventions
+  document's historical baseline says `1.0.0`; the live Dev solution is the
+  authoritative source and must be queried before choosing the version.
+- The checked-in deployment settings are currently empty, so the new Dataverse
+  reference is expected to be the first generated entry.
+- The final ZIP is intentionally ignored by `.gitignore`; the PR carries the

<skill-context name="create-flow">
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\rapha\.copilot\installed-plugins\power-platform-skills\power-automate\skills\create-flow

# Guided Flow Creation Wizard

Walk the user through creating a Power Automate flow step by step.

## Tools

This skill uses the **FlowAgent MCP tools**. Clients surface them with a
client-specific prefix — `mcp__flowagent__<tool>` (Claude Code) or
`flowagent-<tool>` (Copilot CLI) — so they're referred to by bare name below
(e.g. `create_flow`). Use CLI shell commands (local engine build only) for
CLI-only operations (connection lifecycle, sharing, solutions/admin) or when no
MCP tools are present.

## Steps

1. **Gather requirements**: Ask what the flow should do. Identify triggers, actions, connectors.

2. **Select environment**: Call `list_environments` (use `query` to filter). Let user pick or auto-select.

3. **Check for templates**: Call `list_templates`. If a template matches (approval, digest, webhook, etc.), offer to use `scaffold_flow` as a starting point.

4. **Discover connectors**: For each connector, call `get_connector` with `query` to find the operation, then `get_operation_details` for exact parameters. **Never guess parameter names or types.**

5. **Verify connections**: Call `list_connections` filtered by each connector. Confirm Connected status.

6. **Resolve dynamic values**: For params with `dynamicValues`/`dynamicTree` annotations, call `invoke_operation` to get actual values (Teams channels, SharePoint sites, etc.).

7. **Review with user**: Present the flow design. Use AskUserQuestion to confirm trigger, actions, and connections before creating.

8. **Generate definition**: Build following all rules:
   - Always declare `$authentication` (SecureObject) and `$connections` (Object) parameters
   - Use correct action type: `OpenApiConnection` or `OpenApiConnectionWebhook` (from `get_operation_details`)
   - Do NOT include `authentication` in action inputs
   - Use `Embedded` source in connection references
   - HTTP Request triggers require Premium; prefer `Button` kind

9. **Validate**: Call `validate_flow` (and optionally `preflight_flow`) to pre-check. For expressions, look up syntax with `get_expression_help`.

10. **Create**: Call `create_flow` in Stopped state. Report ID and name.

11. **Optionally publish**: Ask if user wants to enable. If yes, call `publish_flow`. For later one-off tweaks, use `edit_flow` (surgical) rather than resending the whole definition.

</skill-context>

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\rapha\.copilot\installed-plugins\power-platform-skills\power-automate\skills\build-flow

# Flow Builder Agent

You are an autonomous Power Automate flow builder agent. Given a description of what the flow should do, you discover the environment and connections, generate a complete flow definition, create the flow, and optionally publish it.

## Input

The user's flow description is: `$ARGUMENTS`

## Tools

This skill uses the **FlowAgent MCP tools**. Clients surface them with a
client-specific prefix — `mcp__flowagent__<tool>` (Claude Code) or
`flowagent-<tool>` (Copilot CLI) — so they're referred to by bare name below
(e.g. `create_flow`). Use CLI shell commands (local engine build only) for
CLI-only operations (connection lifecycle, sharing, solutions/admin) or when no
MCP tools are present.

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `list_environments` | Find environments |
| `get_connector` | Get the operation index for a connector |
| `get_operation_details` | Exact parameter names, types, enums, and required action type |
| `list_connections` | Verify connections exist |
| `resolve_entity` | Resolve display names to IDs (folders, teams, channels, lists, tables) |
| `list_datasets` | Discover datasets for tabular connectors (SharePoint sites, SQL servers, Excel locations) |
| `list_tables` | Discover tables/lists within a dataset (SharePoint lists, SQL tables) |
| `invoke_operation` | Resolve dynamic dropdown/tree values (fallback for connectors not covered above) |
| `get_expression_help` | Look up Logic Apps expression functions + examples |
| `validate_flow` | Pre-flight definition check (offline rules) |
| `preflight_flow` | Multi-signal readiness check (missing refs, solution-wrap) |
| `create_flow` | Create the flow |
| `edit_flow` | Apply surgical action-level edits when iterating |
| `get_flow` | Verify creation |
| `publish_flow` | Enable the flow |
| `scaffold_flow` | Generate from a built-in template |

## Critical Rules

1. **ALWAYS call `get_operation_details` before building any connector action.** Never guess parameter names, enum values, or action types. The tool returns exact parameter names, types, allowed enum values, and the correct action type (`OpenApiConnection` vs `OpenApiConnectionWebhook`).

2. **Use the correct action type.** Standard operations use `OpenApiConnection`. Webhook operations (Approvals `StartAndWaitForAnApproval`, etc.) use `OpenApiConnectionWebhook`. `get_operation_details` returns this in the `actionType` field.

3. **Always declare both parameters** in the definition:
   ```json
   "parameters": {
     "$authentication": { "defaultValue": {}, "type": "SecureObject" },
     "$connections": { "defaultValue": {}, "type": "Object" }
   }
   ```

4. **Do NOT include `authentication` in action inputs.** The Flow API auto-injects it on save.

5. **Use `Embedded` source** in connection references. Never `Invoker`.

6. **HTTP Request triggers (`kind: "Http"`) require Premium.** Use `kind: "Button"` for free/seeded plans.

7. **Validate before creating.** Call `validate_flow` to catch errors before hitting the API.

8. **NEVER use deprecated operations.** Common deprecated operations to avoid:
   - Teams: `PostUserNotification`, `PostChannelNotification`, `PostMessageToChannel`, `PostMessageToChannelV2`, `PostMessageToChannelV3` → use `PostMessageToConversation`
   - Teams: `PostUserAdaptiveCard`, `PostChannelAdaptiveCard` → use `PostCardToConversation`
   - Outlook: `SendEmail` → use `SendEmailV2`; `OnNewEmail`/`OnNewEmailV2` → use `OnNewEmailV3`
   - Approvals: `approvalSubscribeV2` → use `StartAndWaitForAnApproval`
   - Planner: `CreateTask`/`CreateTask_V2` → use `CreateTask_V3`
   - Forms: `GetFormResponses` (polling) → use `CreateFormWebhook` (webhook)

## Workflow

**Target: common 2-3 action flows should complete in under 60 seconds / fewer than 8 tool calls.**

1. **Check for templates FIRST**: Call `list_templates`. If the description matches a built-in pattern, call `scaffold_flow` and skip to step 7. This is the fastest path.

2. **Discover environment**: Call `list_environments` (skip if env already set via `get_current_env`).

3. **Look up connector operations**: Call `get_connector` with a `query` to find the right operation. Verify the operation is NOT deprecated (see rule 8).

4. **Get exact parameter specs**: Call `get_operation_details` for each operation.

5. **Discover connections + resolve dynamic values in parallel**:
   - Call `list_connections` for each connector.
   - Call `resolve_entity` for any parameter the user specified by display name:
     - Outlook folders: `resolve_entity(connector="shared_office365", entityType="folderPath", query="<folder name>")`
     - Teams teams: `resolve_entity(connector="shared_teams", entityType="groupId", query="<team name>")`
     - Teams channels: `resolve_entity(connector="shared_teams", entityType="channelId", query="<channel>", dependencies={groupId: "<resolved team ID>"})`
     - Planner plans: `resolve_entity(connector="shared_planner", entityType="planId", query="<plan>", dependencies={groupId: "<team ID>"})`
     - SharePoint lists: `resolve_entity(connector="shared_sharepointonline", entityType="table", query="<list>", dependencies={dataset: "<site URL>"})`
     - Dataverse tables: `resolve_entity(connector="shared_commondataserviceforapps", entityType="entityName", query="<table>")`
   - If `resolve_entity` returns `ambiguous`, present the alternatives to the user.
   - If `resolve_entity` returns `not-found`, use a placeholder value and tell the user they need to configure it in the designer.
   - **Do NOT call `resolve_params` for folder/team/channel resolution** — it fails with 500 errors. `resolve_entity` uses the API Hub directly and works.

6. **Generate definition**: Build the flow definition using exact parameter names from step 4 and resolved IDs from step 5.

7. **Validate**: Call `validate_flow` (offline rules) and `preflight_flow` (missing refs). Fix errors.

8. **Create flow**: Call `create_flow` in Stopped state.

10. **Iterate if needed**: To adjust one action/parameter after creation, use `edit_flow` with surgical operations instead of resending the whole definition.

11. **Report**: Output flow ID, name, and state.

## Expression Syntax Reference

Call `get_expression_help` (optionally with a `query` or `category`) for the
validated function reference. Common patterns:

- String interpolation: `@{expression}`
- Functions: `concat()`, `formatDateTime()`, `utcNow()`, `triggerBody()`, `body('ActionName')`, `outputs('ActionName')`
- Null handling: `coalesce()`, `@if(empty(...), 'default', ...)`
- `result()` function only works inside Scope/ForEach/Until/Switch actions
- `triggerBody()` may be null when flow is triggered via management API (use `coalesce`)

## AI Builder Prompt Actions

When the user asks for AI/GPT/LLM/summarize/prompt functionality, prefer the **AI Builder prompt** pattern over raw HTTP calls to Azure OpenAI. It uses Copilot credits and requires no API keys.

**Two approaches:**

1. **"Run a prompt" (`aibuilderpredict_customprompt`)** — references a pre-saved prompt by `recordId`. Simpler, but requires the prompt to already exist in AI Builder. Use template `ai-builder-prompt`.

2. **Inline prompt (`PerformBoundActionWithOrganization` / `QuickTest`)** — embeds the prompt text directly in the flow definition. More complex but self-contained.

Both use the Dataverse connector (`shared_commondataserviceforapps`). See `definition-reference.md` for the full action JSON shapes.

**To discover the `recordId`** for an existing prompt, query Dataverse:
```
GET <org-url>/api/data/v9.2/msdyn_aiconfigurations?$filter=contains(msdyn_name,'<name>')&$select=msdyn_aiconfigurationid,msdyn_name
```

**Output expression**: `outputs('Run_a_prompt')?['body/responsev2/predictionOutput/text']`

1. # Poutine League — Architecture
2. 
3. This document describes the initial **Power Platform-centric technical architecture** for Poutine League, derived from the functional vision in [`PRODUCT.md`](./PRODUCT.md). It captures decisions made so far and flags open questions to resolve during implementation.
4. 
5. The architecture leans **exclusively** on four Power Platform building blocks:
6. 
7. | Building block | Role in this product |
8. |---|---|
9. | **Dataverse** | System of record for the data model, plus the mechanism for injecting sample/demo data. |
10. | **Power Automate cloud flows** | Non-AI, deterministic backend processes (scheduling, aggregation, notifications, geocoding). |
11. | **Power Apps code apps** | Front-end experiences (employee app + admin app). |
12. | **Copilot Studio agents (GitHub Copilot harness)** | AI agentic experiences — one interactive conversational agent, and specialized headless agents for backend AI reasoning. |
13. 
14. > [!NOTE]
15. > This document favors a **single Dev environment with one unmanaged solution** for the demo. Multi-environment promotion is intentionally out of scope for the live demo (see [ALM & environments](#alm--environments)), even though a deterministic CD pipeline already exists in this repo as a forward-looking illustration.
16. 
17. ## 1. Data model (Dataverse)
18. 
19. Dataverse is the single system of record. All entities below are custom tables unless noted otherwise.
20. 
21. | Table | Purpose | Key fields (indicative) |
22. |---|---|---|
23. | **Restaurant** | A Montreal restaurant/place where a poutine was found. | Name, address, geocoded latitude/longitude, city area/neighborhood. |
24. | **Poutine Submission** | A submitted poutine, owned by the submitting employee. | Name/description, price, photo (Dataverse file/image column), tags, status (`Draft` → `Submitted` → `In Review` → `Approved`/`Rejected`), lookup to Restaurant, lookup to submitter (system user). |
25. | **Tag** | Descriptive tag (classic, smoked meat, vegan, spicy, …). | Name. Many-to-many with Poutine Submission. |
26. | **Try** | An employee self-declaring they tried a poutine. | Lookup to Poutine Submission, lookup to employee (system user), timestamp. |
27. | **Review** | Rating + comment left after a Try. | Star rating (1–5), comment text, lookup to Try/Poutine Submission, lookup to reviewer (system user), AI-assessed helpfulness score (nullable, populated by the review-scoring backend agent). |
28. | **Season** | A seasonal contest period (winter/spring/summer/autumn). | Start/end date, status (`Active`/`Closed`). |
29. | **Category** | A leaderboard category (Best Seller, Top Poutine, Best Supporter, Best Critic, + future ones). | Name, description, computation type. |
30. | **Season Result** | Persisted, nightly-computed leaderboard standing per season/category. | Lookup to Season, lookup to Category, ranked entries (employee or poutine + score), computed-at timestamp. |
31. | **Hall of Fame Entry** | All-time winners, archived at season close. | Lookup to Season, lookup to Category, winner (employee or poutine), badge/title text. |
32. 
33. **Employees are Dataverse system users backed by Entra ID** — no custom Employee table. Submissions, tries, and reviews are attributed via lookups to `systemuser`, keeping identity/auth outside the app's data model.
34. 
35. ### Entity relationship diagram
36. 
37. ```mermaid
38. erDiagram
39.     SYSTEMUSER ||--o{ POUTINE_SUBMISSION : "submits"
40.     SYSTEMUSER ||--o{ TRY : "tries"
41.     SYSTEMUSER ||--o{ REVIEW : "reviews"
42. 
43.     RESTAURANT ||--o{ POUTINE_SUBMISSION : "serves"
44. 
45.     POUTINE_SUBMISSION ||--o{ TRY : "is tried via"
46.     POUTINE_SUBMISSION }o--o{ TAG : "tagged with"
47. 
48.     TRY ||--o| REVIEW : "rated by"
49. 
50.     SEASON ||--o{ SEASON_RESULT : "scoped to"
51.     CATEGORY ||--o{ SEASON_RESULT : "ranked by"
52.     SEASON ||--o{ HALL_OF_FAME_ENTRY : "archives into"
53.     CATEGORY ||--o{ HALL_OF_FAME_ENTRY : "crowns"
54. 
55.     SYSTEMUSER {
56.         guid systemuserid PK
57.         string fullname
58.         string email
59.     }
60. 
61.     RESTAURANT {
62.         guid restaurantid PK
63.         string name
64.         string address
65.         decimal latitude
66.         decimal longitude
67.     }
68. 
69.     POUTINE_SUBMISSION {
70.         guid poutinesubmissionid PK
71.         guid restaurantid FK
72.         guid submitterid FK
73.         string name
74.         string description
75.         decimal price
76.         image photo
77.         choice status "Draft, Submitted, In Review, Approved, Rejected"
78.     }
79. 
80.     TAG {
81.         guid tagid PK
82.         string name
83.     }
84. 
85.     TRY {
86.         guid tryid PK
87.         guid poutinesubmissionid FK
88.         guid employeeid FK
89.         datetime triedon
90.     }
91. 
92.     REVIEW {
93.         guid reviewid PK
94.         guid tryid FK
95.         guid reviewerid FK
96.         int starrating "1-5"
97.         string comment
98.         decimal helpfulnessscore "AI-assessed, nullable"
99.     }
100. 
101.     SEASON {
102.         guid seasonid PK
103.         string name
104.         date startdate
105.         date enddate
106.         choice status "Active, Closed"
107.     }
108. 
109.     CATEGORY {
110.         guid categoryid PK
111.         string name
112.         string computationtype
113.     }
114. 
115.     SEASON_RESULT {
116.         guid seasonresultid PK

118.         guid categoryid FK
119.         datetime computedat
120.     }
121.

127.     }
128. ```
129. 
130. > [!NOTE]
131. > `SYSTEMUSER` is Dataverse's built-in table (not custom) — shown here only to make the identity relationships explicit. `POUTINE_SUBMISSION` ↔ `TAG` is a many-to-many relationship (native Dataverse N:N).
132. 
133. ### Security roles
134. 
135. - **Admin/Moderator**: a small group (2–3 people) using the built-in **System Administrator** security role — acceptable at this scale/org, keeps setup simple, no custom role needed.
136. - **Employee**: follows the **principle of least privilege** — read access to all public data (submissions, reviews, leaderboards), write access scoped to their own submissions/tries/reviews only. Exact field- and record-level privileges to be defined as a custom security role when building the code apps.
137. 
138. ### Confirmed decisions
139. 
140. - **Restaurant stays normalized as its own table** (as modeled above) — gives a cleaner data model, clear separation of concerns per table, and enables future capabilities like tracking which restaurants keep appearing across seasons.
141. - **`Season Result` stores a full ranked-list snapshot per season/category**, not just the top-1 winner — even though only the top-1 is announced/crowned at season close, the fuller snapshot supports richer leaderboard history and analytics later.
142. - **The ranked-entries list is implemented as a child table, `Season Result Entry`** (lookup to Season Result, rank, score, and *either* an employee lookup *or* a Poutine Submission lookup depending on the category's computation type) — since Dataverse cannot store an array inside a single row. This is a relational-decomposition implementation detail of the `Season Result` row above, not new business scope.
143. 
144. > [!NOTE]
145. > The `Season Result Entry` child table was introduced autonomously by an agent session in the human's absence, to make the "ranked entries" concept concrete in Dataverse. Flagged here for human review — a different representation (e.g. JSON blob, fixed top-N columns) can still be adopted if preferred.
146. 
147. ## 2. AI agentic experiences (Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot harness)
148. 
149. All Copilot Studio agents in this product are built on the **[GitHub Copilot harness](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/harnesses-overview)** (no classic "topics" — reasoning-driven, tool/knowledge/connected-agent orchestration).
150. 
151. ### 2.1 Interactive conversational agent (single entry point)
152. 
153. One agent serves as the **single conversational entry point** for employees — submitting/managing poutines, exploring poutines to try, and checking the leaderboard, all through natural-language interaction. It is:
154. 
155. - **Embedded inside the employee-facing code app** (chat panel), and
156. - **Also published standalone to Microsoft 365 Copilot**,
157. 
158. so employees can reach it from either surface. It uses Dataverse as a tool/knowledge source to read and write submissions, tries, and reviews on the user's behalf, respecting the same security roles as the code app.
159. 
160. ### 2.2 Specialized backend agents (headless, non-interactive)
161. 
162. Backend AI reasoning is split into **specialized agents**, each with a narrow responsibility, invoked as backend processes rather than through chat:
163. 
164. | Backend agent | Responsibility | Triggered by |
165. |---|---|---|
166. | **Submission Review agent** | Combines completeness check, duplicate/similarity detection (same restaurant/very similar poutine), and first-pass moderation; escalates ambiguous cases instead of deciding blindly. | Poutine Submission status change `Draft` → `Submitted` (see [submission flow](#3-submission-review-flow)). |
167. | **Fun Facts agent** | Generates engaging trivia/context about an approved poutine or restaurant, grounded in Dataverse data (submission details, tags, restaurant info) and the model's general knowledge — **no external web search grounding**, to keep the demo self-contained. | Poutine Submission reaching `Approved` status; may also be reused on-demand as a connected-agent tool by the interactive agent when an employee asks for a fun fact in chat. |
168. | **Review Quality agent** | Scores review helpfulness/insightfulness to power the "Best Critic" category. | Nightly leaderboard computation flow (§4). |
169. 
170. > [!NOTE]
171. > **Multi-agent design follows Microsoft's guidance**: keep it to one interactive agent as the default entry point, and only split into specialized agents where there's a distinct domain, distinct trigger, or reusability need — which is the case for review, fun facts, and review-quality scoring.
172. 
173. ## 3. Submission review flow
174. 
175. 1. An employee starts a **Poutine Submission** in `Draft` status via the employee code app (or the conversational agent).
176. 2. When ready, they move it to `Submitted`.
177. 3. The **Submission Review agent** is invoked from a **Power Automate cloud flow** triggered on that Dataverse status change, and performs completeness + duplicate/similarity + first-pass moderation checks.
178. 4. Clear-cut outcomes move the record straight to `Approved` or `Rejected`.
179. 5. Ambiguous cases are flagged `In Review` and escalated to a human moderator/admin.
180. 
181. ### Escalation mechanism (open question — see below)
182. 
183. - **Primary (aspirational)**: use Copilot Studio's **[Request for Information (RFI)](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/blog/copilot-studio/introducing-request-for-information-in-copilot-studio-agent-flows/)** human-in-the-loop node inside a **Copilot Studio Workflow**, emailing the moderator a structured form and feeding the response back into the flow.
184. - **Fallback (primary for the demo)**: flag the Dataverse record `In Review`, surface it in the **admin code app**'s review queue, and send a lightweight **Microsoft Teams heads-up notification** via Power Automate.
185. 
186. > [!IMPORTANT]
187. > Copilot Studio **Workflows** are not yet supported by the Copilot Studio-related skills/plugins used in this repo (`skills-for-copilot-studio`, `copilot-studio-plugin`). Until that changes, **Power Automate cloud flows call specialized Copilot Studio agents directly** via the **[Microsoft Copilot Studio connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/microsoftcopilotstudio/)** as the one consistent AI-invocation pattern across the product. Adopting Copilot Studio Workflows (and the RFI node) for the submission-review escalation is a **future exploration to keep an eye on** as Microsoft's tooling evolves — it is not expected to land in time for this demo.
188. 
189. ## 4. Non-AI backend processes (Power Automate cloud flows)
190. 
191. | Flow | Purpose | Trigger |
192. |---|---|---|
193. | **Submission review orchestration** | Calls the Submission Review agent (**[Execute Agent and wait](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/microsoftcopilotstudio/#execute-agent-and-wait)** — needs the agent's decision synchronously to apply it to the record) and applies its outcome to the Dataverse record. | Dataverse: Poutine Submission status → `Submitted`. |
194. | **Geocoding** | Resolves a submitted restaurant address to latitude/longitude for the map view, using the free tier of [geocod.io](https://www.geocod.io/free-geocoding). | Dataverse: new/updated Restaurant address. |
195. | **Fun facts generation** | Calls the Fun Facts agent (**[Execute Agent and wait](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/microsoftcopilotstudio/#execute-agent-and-wait)**) and stores the result once a submission is approved. | Dataverse: Poutine Submission status → `Approved`. |
196. | **Nightly leaderboard computation** | Recomputes and persists standings for all live categories (including calling the Review Quality agent — **[Execute Agent and wait](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/microsoftcopilotstudio/#execute-agent-and-wait)** — for Best Critic) into `Season Result`. | Scheduled (nightly). |
197. | **Season rollover** | Closes the active season, crowns the top-1 winner per category, archives to `Hall of Fame Entry`, opens the next season. | Scheduled (quarterly/date-based, aligned to season boundaries). |
198. | **Winner announcement notification** | Notifies employees of season results and category winners. | Triggered by the season rollover flow; delivered via **Microsoft Teams**. |
199. 
200. Live leaderboard views inside the code apps are **computed on demand by the code app** from raw Dataverse data (ratings, tries, reviews) for responsiveness; the nightly flow's persisted `Season Result` snapshot is the durable, "official" record used for history, badges, and season-close/Hall of Fame purposes.
201. 
202. > [!NOTE]
203. > All flow → agent calls use the **[Microsoft Copilot Studio connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/microsoftcopilotstudio/)**. Use **[Execute Agent and wait](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/microsoftcopilotstudio/#execute-agent-and-wait)** when the flow needs the agent's response synchronously to continue (all cases above); the fire-and-forget **[Execute Agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/microsoftcopilotstudio/#execute-agent)** action remains available for any future scenario that doesn't need to block on a response.
204. 
205. ## 5. Front-end experiences (Power Apps code apps)
206. 
207. Two separate code apps, both connecting to Dataverse:
208. 
209. 1. **Employee app** — submit/manage poutines (respecting the 5 active-submission cap), browse/discover (list + map views, using an open-source JS map library such as Leaflet with geocoded coordinates from Dataverse), mark poutines as tried, leave reviews, view leaderboards and Hall of Fame, and access the embedded conversational agent.
210. 2. **Admin/moderation app** — review queue for escalated submissions, override approve/reject decisions, manage categories/seasons, and any other admin utilities.
211. 
212. ## 6. Sample/demo data
213. 
214. Dataverse also serves as the target for **sample data injection** used for testing and demos: seed data (restaurants, poutines, tags, reviews, seasons) is authored as CSV/JSON files in the repo and loaded via the **Dataverse skill's bulk/data import capability**, keeping seeding reproducible and reviewable in source control rather than a one-off script or flow.
215. 
216. ## 7. ALM & environments
217. 
218. - **Primary focus for this architecture and the live demo: a single Dev environment with one unmanaged solution.** All components (tables, flows, code apps, agents) live in this one solution during active development.
219. - The repo already includes a forward-looking, deterministic CD pipeline (`.github/workflows/deploy-solution.yml`) that packs and imports changed solutions to a target environment via PAC CLI + OIDC on merges to `main`. It's meant to **illustrate** the target promotion pattern — keeping deployment deterministic and human-reviewed through PRs — rather than to be exercised live during the demo.
220. - Multi-environment promotion (Dev → Test/Prod), managed vs. unmanaged solution strategy at scale, and connection reference/environment variable management across environments are **explicitly deferred** — see the `solution-management` skill for the mechanics when this becomes relevant.

1. # Makefile — local developer tooling for Power Apps code apps and Power Platform solutions.
2. # Targets operate on directories discovered at runtime so no file changes are needed when
3. # new apps/solutions are added.
4. 
5. .DEFAULT_GOAL := help
6. 
7. APP ?=
8. SOLUTION ?=
9. CHECKER_GEO ?= UnitedStates
10. 
11. # Discover all first-level subdirectories and sort for deterministic output/order.
12. # Exclude dotdirs (e.g. code-apps/.impeccable, the shared design-hook config) — they
13. # are not code apps and have no package.json to lint/test/build.
14. CODE_APPS := $(shell find code-apps -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name '.*' 2>/dev/null | sort)
15. SOLUTIONS := $(shell find solutions -maxdepth 1 -mindepth 1 -type d ! -name '.*' 2>/dev/null | sort)
16. 
17. .PHONY: help \
18. 	app-lint app-test app-build app-gate \
19. 	solution-pack solution-check solution-gate solution-sync \
20. 	entire-observe entire-link-dry entire-link-apply entire-link-apply-unsafe entire-stack-finalize
21. 
22. ## help: list available targets with descriptions and examples
23. help:
24. 	@echo ""
25. 	@echo "Available targets:"
26. 	@echo "  app-lint          Lint all code apps (or one with APP=<name>)"
27. 	@echo "  app-test          Test all code apps (or one with APP=<name>)"
28. 	@echo "  app-build         Build all code apps (or one with APP=<name>)"
29. 	@echo "  app-gate          Mandatory pre-push app gate: app-lint + app-test"
30. 	@echo "  solution-pack     Pack all solutions (or one with SOLUTION=<name>)"
31. 	@echo "  solution-check    Run Solution Checker on all solutions (or one with SOLUTION=<name>)"
32. 	@echo "  solution-gate     Mandatory solution gate: solution-pack + solution-check"
33. 	@echo "  solution-sync     If SOLUTION exists locally: sync; otherwise: clone it"
34. 	@echo ""
35. 	@echo "Examples:"
36. 	@echo "  make app-lint"
37. 	@echo "  APP=my-app make app-test"
38. 	@echo "  APP=my-app make app-build"
39. 	@echo "  make app-gate"
40. 	@echo "  make solution-pack"
41. 	@echo "  SOLUTION=CorePlatform make solution-pack"
42. 	@echo "  SOLUTION=CorePlatform make solution-check CHECKER_GEO=Europe"
43. 	@echo "  SOLUTION=CorePlatform make solution-sync"
44. 	@echo "  make solution-gate"
45. 	@echo ""
46. 
47. ## app-lint: run 'npm run lint' inside each selected code app directory
48. app-lint:
49. 	@if [ -n "$(APP)" ] && [ ! -d "code-apps/$(APP)" ]; then \
50. 		echo "Code app '$(APP)' not found under code-apps/."; \
51. 		exit 1; \
52. 	fi
53. 	@APPS="$(CODE_APPS)"; \
54. 	if [ -n "$(APP)" ]; then APPS="code-apps/$(APP)"; fi; \
55. 	if [ -z "$$APPS" ]; then \
56. 		echo "No code apps found under code-apps/ — skipping app-lint."; \
57. 	else \
58. 		# set -e stops on first app failure so CI exits non-zero immediately. \
59. 		set -e; \
60. 		for app in $$APPS; do \
61. 			echo "==> Linting $$app"; \
62. 			(cd "$$app" && npm run lint); \
63. 		done; \
64. 	fi
65. 
66. ## app-test: run 'npm test' inside each selected code app directory
67. app-test:
68. 	@if [ -n "$(APP)" ] && [ ! -d "code-apps/$(APP)" ]; then \
69. 		echo "Code app '$(APP)' not found under code-apps/."; \
70. 		exit 1; \
71. 	fi
72. 	@APPS="$(CODE_APPS)"; \
73. 	if [ -n "$(APP)" ]; then APPS="code-apps/$(APP)"; fi; \
74. 	if [ -z "$$APPS" ]; then \
75. 		echo "No code apps found under code-apps/ — skipping app-test."; \
76. 	else \
77. 		set -e; \
78. 		for app in $$APPS; do \
79. 			echo "==> Testing $$app"; \
80. 			(cd "$$app" && npm test); \
81. 		done; \
82. 	fi
83. 
84. ## app-build: run 'npm run build' inside each selected code app directory
85. app-build:
86. 	@if [ -n "$(APP)" ] && [ ! -d "code-apps/$(APP)" ]; then \
87. 		echo "Code app '$(APP)' not found under code-apps/."; \
88. 		exit 1; \
89. 	fi
90. 	@APPS="$(CODE_APPS)"; \
91. 	if [ -n "$(APP)" ]; then APPS="code-apps/$(APP)"; fi; \
92. 	if [ -z "$$APPS" ]; then \
93. 		echo "No code apps found under code-apps/ — skipping app-build."; \
94. 	else \
95. 		set -e; \
96. 		for app in $$APPS; do \
97. 			echo "==> Building $$app"; \
98. 			(cd "$$app" && npm run build); \
99. 		done; \
100. 	fi
101. 
102. ## app-gate: mandatory pre-push gate for code apps
103. app-gate: app-lint app-test
104. 
105. ## solution-pack: structural pack check for each selected solution
106. solution-pack:
107. 	@if ! command -v pac >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
108. 		echo "pac CLI not found — skipping solution-pack. Install from https://aka.ms/PowerAppsCLI"; \
109. 		exit 0; \
110. 	fi
111. 	@if [ -n "$(SOLUTION)" ] && [ ! -d "solutions/$(SOLUTION)" ]; then \
112. 		echo "Solution '$(SOLUTION)' not found under solutions/."; \
113. 		exit 1; \
114. 	fi
115. 	@SOLS="$(SOLUTIONS)"; \
116. 	if [ -n "$(SOLUTION)" ]; then SOLS="solutions/$(SOLUTION)"; fi; \
117. 	if [ -z "$$SOLS" ]; then \
118. 		echo "No solutions found under solutions/ — skipping solution-pack."; \
119. 	else \
120. 		set -e; \
121. 		for sol in $$SOLS; do \
122. 			echo "==> Packing $$sol (structural check)"; \
123. 			# Pack to a temp zip; delete immediately so no pack artifact lands in git status. \
124. 			tmp=$$(mktemp /tmp/pack-XXXXXX.zip); \
125. 			pac solution pack --folder "$$sol" --zipfile "$$tmp" --processCanvasApps; \
126. 			rm -f "$$tmp"; \
127. 		done; \
128. 	fi
129. 
130. ## solution-check: run Power Apps Solution Checker for each selected solution
131. solution-check:
132. 	@if ! command -v pac >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
133. 		echo "pac CLI not found — skipping solution-check. Install from https://aka.ms/PowerAppsCLI"; \
134. 		exit 0; \
135. 	fi
136. 	@if [ -n "$(SOLUTION)" ] && [ ! -d "solutions/$(SOLUTION)" ]; then \
137. 		echo "Solution '$(SOLUTION)' not found under solutions/."; \
138. 		exit 1; \
139. 	fi
140. 	@SOLS="$(SOLUTIONS)"; \
141. 	if [ -n "$(SOLUTION)" ]; then SOLS="solutions/$(SOLUTION)"; fi; \
142. 	if [ -z "$$SOLS" ]; then \
143. 		echo "No solutions found under solutions/ — skipping solution-check."; \
144. 	else \
145. 		set -e; \
146. 		for sol in $$SOLS; do \
147. 			echo "==> Running solution checker for $$sol"; \
148. 			# The checker consumes zip input, so pack to a temp workspace and clean it after use. \
149. 			tmpdir=$$(mktemp -d); \
150. 			zipfile="$$tmpdir/$$(basename "$$sol").zip"; \
151. 			output="$$tmpdir/checker-output"; \
152. 			pac solution pack --folder "$$sol" --zipfile "$$zipfile" --processCanvasApps; \
153. 			pac solution check --path "$$zipfile" --outputDirectory "$$output" --geo "$(CHECKER_GEO)"; \
154. 			rm -rf "$$tmpdir"; \
155. 		done; \
156. 	fi
157. 
158. ## solution-gate: mandatory gate for solutions
159. solution-gate: solution-pack solution-check
160. 
161. ## solution-sync: clone a missing solution folder or sync an existing one
162. solution-sync:
163. 	@if ! command -v pac >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
164. 		echo "pac CLI not found — skipping solution-sync. Install from https://aka.ms/PowerAppsCLI"; \
165. 		exit 0; \
166. 	fi
167. 	@mkdir -p solutions
168. 	@if [ -n "$(SOLUTION)" ]; then \
169. 		if [ -d "solutions/$(SOLUTION)" ]; then \
170. 			echo "==> Syncing existing solution solutions/$(SOLUTION)"; \
171. 			pac solution sync --solution-folder "solutions/$(SOLUTION)"; \
172. 		else \
173. 			echo "==> Cloning missing solution $(SOLUTION) into solutions/$(SOLUTION)"; \
174. 			pac solution clone --name "$(SOLUTION)" --outputDirectory "solutions/$(SOLUTION)"; \
175. 		fi; \
176. 	elif [ -z "$(SOLUTIONS)" ]; then \
177. 		echo "No local solutions found. Use SOLUTION=<name> make solution-sync to clone one."; \
178. 	else \
179. 		set -e; \
180. 		for sol in $(SOLUTIONS); do \
181. 			echo "==> Syncing $$sol"; \
182. 			pac solution sync --solution-folder "$$sol"; \
183. 		done; \
184. 	fi
185. 
186. ## entire-observe: capture Entire/Copilot observability snapshot (experimental, non-destructive)
187. entire-observe:
188. 	@powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/entire-integration/Invoke-EntireObservability.ps1 -Stage manual
189. 
190. ## entire-link-dry: print experimental session-linking plan without mutating commits
191. entire-link-dry:
192. 	@powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/entire-integration/Invoke-EntireExperimentalLink.ps1
193. 
194. ## entire-link-apply: apply experimental session attach (explicitly destructive)
195. entire-link-apply:
196. 	@powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/entire-integration/Invoke-EntireExperimentalLink.ps1 -Apply
197. 
198. ## entire-link-apply-unsafe: bypass confidence gate (requires SESSION_ID=<id>)
199. entire-link-apply-unsafe:
200. 	@if [ -z "$(SESSION_ID)" ]; then \
201. 		echo "SESSION_ID is required. Example: make entire-link-apply-unsafe SESSION_ID=<copilot-session-id>"; \
202. 		exit 1; \
203. 	fi
204. 	@powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/entire-integration/Invoke-EntireExperimentalLink.ps1 -Apply -AllowLowConfidence -SessionId "$(SESSION_ID)"
205. 
206. ## entire-stack-finalize: run experimental trailer audit/finalization on current branch
207. entire-stack-finalize:
208. 	@powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/entire-integration/Invoke-EntireStackFinalize.ps1
